shown:
── NESSA'S WEEK ──
Nessa is 41 and new to running, aiming to run the whole Corrowmore Harvest 5K on 15 November without walking. Nessa walk-runs three mornings a week (Monday, Wednesday and Saturday) and walks the dog most days.
Recent weeks: 6.8, 7.3 km
This week: 2.8 km over 1 run. Missed 2 of 3 planned runs.
Body: "Came down with a cold on Tuesday that turned into a fever, 38.4 on Wednesday night. No fever since Friday but still coughing and blocked up."
Feeling: "Wiped out."
Asks: "Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Nessa: Ease back in after the fever. …
Answers: (1) No, don't add the two missed runs. Running hard to catch up is the most common way to turn a cold into a longer layoff, and a few days off costs you very little at this stage. (2) You will still have three sessions on your usual Monday, Wednesday and Saturday mornings. Only two are runs, and neither is longer than what you have already done.
Safety flag: Get the cough checked if it lingers
Next week:
Mon: other, 25 min, easy walk with the dog and no running, at a pace where you can chat…
Tue: rest. Sleep matters more than training while the cough clears.
Wed: easy, 20 min, 5 min brisk walk then 5 x 2 min easy run and 1 min walk, heart rate…
Thu: rest. Dog walks are fine.
Fri: rest. Dog walks are fine, and a good night's sleep is the aim.
Sat: easy, 24 min, 8 x 2 min easy run and 1 min walk, effort 4–5/10, and only if…
Sun: rest. Dog walk only, so you start the next week fresh.
